name: Pfrillsee Kufstein
kurzbeschreibung: The peaceful Pfrillsee, nestled between Kufstein and Thiersee, is a hidden gem for nature lovers.
preis: Kostenlos frei zugänglich (Parkplatz Hechtsee ca. 3–5 € pro Tag)
beschreibung:
Overview

Lake Pfrillsee is the smallest, highest, and warmest of the four celebrated woodland lakes ringing Kufstein (alongside Hechtsee, Egelsee, and Längsee). Nestled peacefully at 615 meters elevation within a protected forest depression beneath the wooded Thierberg hill, this pristine body of water spans roughly 1.7 hectares with depths reaching eight meters. As a preserved moorland lake, Pfrillsee is characterized by soft, dark, mineral-rich peat water that warms quickly under early summer sunshine, welcoming wild swimmers and solace seekers. Fringed by fragrant mixed deciduous woods, reed belts, and white water lily colonies, the lake offers an idyllic sanctuary sheltered from urban commotion. A cherished landmark along the classic Kufstein Four Lakes Circuit, it provides sanctuary for protected dragonflies, grass snakes, and aquatic birds.

Route & Requirements

Excursions around Pfrillsee range from brief forest strolls to extended day circuits connecting neighboring lakes. The immediate shoreline loop traces gentle woodland singletrack and boardwalk sections circling the water in approximately 20 to 30 minutes (distance approx. 1.2 km, easy grade T1, family-friendly; exposed tree roots make it less suitable for standard strollers). Several timber docks and sunny secluded clearings invite peaceful wild swimming. Walkers frequently combine Pfrillsee with Lake Hechtsee and Längsee: starting from the main Hechtsee car park, a signposted forest trail climbs gently through beech and spruce canopies to reach Pfrillsee in roughly 45 minutes (round-trip 1.5 hours, 120 vertical meters gain, easy grade T1). Sturdy walking shoes with reliable grip are recommended, especially following rainfall. Leashed dogs are welcome on all surrounding woodland trails.

Visit & Arrival

Rail transit arrives via mainline ÖBB or German regional trains at Kufstein central station. From there, local city buses connect toward Kufstein-Zell or Morsbach, with marked walking paths climbing from the town center to the lake in about 45 minutes. Motorists take the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Kufstein-Nord) and leave vehicles at the Hechtsee hiker parking lot or along designated laybys off the Thiersee provincial road L37. Lake Pfrillsee is open year-round with completely free public access.

Tips

Arrive in the early morning hours when delicate mist ribbons float across the dark glassy surface reflecting surrounding evergreen canopies—a tranquil oasis for landscape photographers. Combine your visit with a brief ascent to the nearby medieval ruins of Thierberg Castle and its panoramic observation tower.
saison: Ganzjährig frei zugänglich (Badesaison Juni bis September)
